questions.question: Which family of status codes means the client made a mistake in the request?
questions.explanation: 4xx codes are client errors, such as 400 Bad Request and 404 Not Found. 5xx codes mean the server failed.

questions.question: A client is logged in but tries to open a page it has no permission for. Which status fits best?
questions.explanation: 403 means the client is known but not allowed. 401 means the client is not authenticated.

questions.question: A method has @PostMapping and @ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.CREATED) and returns normally. What status does the client see?
questions.explanation: @ResponseStatus replaces the default 200 with the status you choose, here 201 Created.

questions.question: A controller throws RideNotFoundException, and a @RestControllerAdvice has @ExceptionHandler for it that returns ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND). What does the client get?
options: 404 Not Found with the handler's body
questions.explanation: The handler catches the exception and builds the reply, so the client gets 404 with the body the handler returns.

questions.question: An API returns status 200 with the body {"error":"Seat already booked"}. What is wrong?
options: JSON cannot contain the word error
The status should be 409, because clients check the status code first
The body should be plain text
questions.explanation: A failure must be shown in the status code. A clash with existing data is a 409 Conflict.
